core_obligations: Set up the geometric points (proof lines 19310-19314): denote by sbar' and sbar the images of xbar' and xbar in S' and S, and let tbar' be a geometric point of Spec(O^{sh}_{S',sbar'}) with image tbar in Spec(O^{sh}_{S,sbar}).

Compare strict henselizations (proof lines 19315-19324): under the three alternative hypotheses on g, the cited Algebra result gives that O^{sh}_{X,xbar} tensor over O^{sh}_{S,sbar} with O^{sh}_{S',sbar'} maps isomorphically to O^{sh}_{X',xbar'}.

Identify the vanishing cycles (proof lines 19325-19339): since kappa(tbar) = kappa(tbar'), the displayed chain of equalities shows F_{xbar',tbar'} = F_{xbar,tbar}, so the varieties of vanishing cycles of f' at xbar' are among those of f at xbar.
Conclude (proof lines 19340-19343): local acyclicity of f' at xbar' relative to (g')^{-1}K follows immediately from this identification and the definitions.
proof_roadmap: Choose a geometric point over the strict henselization of S' at sbar' and its image over that of S at sbar.
Use the strict henselization comparison to rewrite the base of the vanishing cycles of f' as a base of the vanishing cycles of f.
Identify the two vanishing cycle varieties.
Read local acyclicity of f' off the hypothesis on f.
difficulty_reason: The lemma propagates local acyclicity across a cartesian square: if f is locally acyclic at xbar relative to K and g is quasi-finite, or a directed limit of locally quasi-finite schemes with affine transitions, or integral, then f' is locally acyclic at xbar' relative to (g')^{-1}K (statement lines 19288-19307). The proof is a comparison of strict henselizations: under the hypotheses on g the tensor product O^{sh}_{X,xbar} tensor_{O^{sh}_{S,sbar}} O^{sh}_{S',sbar'} is O^{sh}_{X',xbar'} (proof lines 19315-19324), and since kappa(tbar) = kappa(tbar') the two varieties of vanishing cycles coincide term by term in the displayed chain (proof lines 19325-19339), so the vanishing cycles of f' are instances of those of f and the definition gives the conclusion. The non-formal content is the correct identification of the vanishing cycle varieties. The claim is H2: one ring-theoretic comparison plus one identification of spectra.
